observations.scope_boundary: M6.9 originally allowed changes only to isolated routed 8216 and account-router private configuration. During r18 the user explicitly interrupted and authorized a minimal standalone 8215 repair; the exception was limited to immutable startup/static-delivery successors and the stdout log boundary. The user later explicitly authorized changing 8215 to a newly device-authorized account, then explicitly authorized an 8215-only Codex Full Access override while requiring 8216 to remain unchanged. During r21 the user explicitly requested a parallel subagent repair for a stuck 8215 startup page; that subagent restarted only the standalone Web process and installed a standalone lifecycle drop-in, while the primary r21 deployment subsequently captured and preserved the fresh 8215 baseline. The standalone credential remains isolated from the router. The 8214 deployment remained out of scope.

standalone_8215_scope_override.expected_result: Restore signed-in standalone 8215 browser and model use, reduce the uncompressed startup transfer, prevent future verbose IPC/model stdout from entering the journal, activate the separately authorized standalone account without enrolling it into the router, and later give only its Codex App Server Full Access without modifying 8216.

blockers: The second user-authorized credential is isolated to standalone 8215. Explicit authorization to enroll it into the router is still required before the real new-request A-to-B E2E, two-binding restart verification and provider-level failover proof can run.
residual_risks: Cross-account continuity remains unverified and is not claimed.

Pre-fix codex-web-router journal records may contain upstream IPC bodies or response headers. Per-unit deletion is unavailable without vacuuming unrelated system logs; retention and access must be handled operationally.

Release r17 removes the separate startup-shim revalidation request, r18 compresses final HTML, r19 reduces the Brotli main bundle by 120417 bytes, and r20 makes the preload content-hash URL immutable, but live usable-screen observations remain variable and do not prove a stable end-to-end speedup.

Standalone 8215 journal records created before its new stdout boundary may contain upstream IPC bodies. Per-unit deletion is unavailable without vacuuming unrelated system logs; retention and access must be handled operationally.
The main bundle remains 3.174 MB over Brotli and 13.936 MB decoded; transfer, parse and renderer work remain the dominant likely optimization area without a safe upstream chunk boundary.
The App Server timing probe shows its initialization and sampled methods are not the remaining multi-second startup component, but it does not prove an exact browser critical-path breakdown.
Browser control plugin instrumentation errors were distinct from the served page and were excluded from codex-web performance evidence.
Direct Tailnet HTTP still requires a browser compatibility shim; HTTPS remains preferable.
Every authorized Tailnet principal reaching 8216 can use the configured routed accounts and workspace authority.

Standalone 8215 now deliberately runs Codex with danger-full-access and without the outer systemd filesystem/network sandbox. Any prompt injection or malicious repository content can access everything available to the unprivileged codex Unix account; root/passwordless sudo was not granted.
R21 now accepts the exact HTTP/SSE path that previously returned HTTP 405, but no post-R21 real title-generation request was sent; model-manager refreshes can time out and were not rechecked.
